benchmark.category: a virtual LARP-gear try-on and AI stylist with a sample marketplace catalog
benchmark.users: LARP and costume shoppers on a hackathon demo who upload a selfie, enter measurements and try gear on a generated model

requirements.source_phrase: Every piece shown on the person should correspond to a specific available listing.
requirements.statement: POST /api/fitting-room/tryon accepts the equipped item_ids array, resolves each id against the sample catalog and uses those items in the generated photo; if any id is unknown or not available in the marketplace it returns HTTP 409 with an error naming that id and generates no image, so no piece outside the available catalog is ever rendered
requirements.notes: The new window adds availability and the 409 contract; the build's known 'silently omits' issue is covered separately by tryon-omitted-be.

requirements.source_phrase: Include an AI assistant that users can talk or chat with to request changes and see the preview update.
requirements.statement: Typing a message into ai-stylist-input and sending shows the assistant reply in the chat, and every equip, unequip, remove, set-aside/swap, filter or style_note the reply carries is applied to the outfit list, the worn set and the next preview in the same turn
requirements.notes: The new window adds remove and swap to the assistant's change set; a reply that renders but changes nothing is still a finding.

requirements.source_phrase: The Quartermaster should only suggest items available in the marketplace.
requirements.statement: POST /api/fitting-room/assistant accepts {message, history, equipped_ids, benched_ids, filters, style_note} and returns reply, equip, unequip, remove, filters, style_note and highlight, where every id in equip, unequip, remove and highlight is a catalog item marked available in the marketplace and an unknown request yields a reply naming an available alternative and no invented id
requirements.notes: Contract expands the inherited version with benched_ids, remove[] and availability; the build description names benched_ids and remove[]. Fit filtering is a separate requirement.

requirements.source_phrase: Also allow users to continue making these changes with voice commands or text.
requirements.statement: Every assistant capability (equip, unequip, remove, set aside/swap, filter, style change) is reachable by typed chat from ai-stylist-input without a microphone, and where speech recognition is available the same changes can be issued by voice through a visible microphone control; a missing microphone, denied permission or unsupported browser leaves typed chat fully working and does not block the core flow
requirements.notes: The new window asks for voice as well as text, superseding the earlier typed-first preference. Chrome-only voice is verified by code review because it cannot be driven headlessly per the agent context note.

requirements.source_phrase: The Quartermaster should only suggest items available in the marketplace.
requirements.statement: A request for an item with no catalog match (for example a purple lightsaber) returns reply text saying the item is unavailable and naming at least one available catalog listing as an alternative, with no invented id in equip, highlight or remove
requirements.notes: The new window's example adds a not-in-catalog request; the alternative must itself be an available catalog id.

requirements.source_phrase: Display all selected items beneath the search, with their prices and other details.
requirements.statement: Once items are selected, an outfit list appears directly beneath catalog-search-input and lists every worn and set-aside item with its name, price, size and seller, a count, and per-item controls to open the item, toggle it between worn and set-aside, and remove it from the outfit
requirements.notes: The new window states this as a fixed requirement; the build places data-testid outfit-list directly under catalog-search-input and shows worn + set-aside rows. Size and seller are the 'other details' from the build description.

requirements.source_phrase: When a user adds a selfie, require them to enter their height, weight, and gender
requirements.statement: After a selfie is accepted, a measurements dialog appears and the model and preview are not finalized until height, weight and gender are entered; closing or bypassing the dialog without all three values leaves the user in the dialog and generates nothing
requirements.notes: The user's word 'require' makes the gate non-skippable; the build implements it as a dialog that cannot be dismissed. Phase 4 uploads /app/tests/selfie.jpg through the file input and should assert the dialog remains until all three values are saved.

requirements.source_phrase: When a user adds a selfie, require them to enter their height, weight, and gender
requirements.statement: The server accepts a session measurement profile of height, weight and gender/fit, refuses a profile with a missing, non-numeric or non-positive height or weight or an unrecognised gender, and supplies only a validated profile to catalog filtering, try-on and assistant requests so no generated model is produced for an invalid profile
requirements.notes: Validation must exist server-side because the flow has no auth and a direct API call bypasses the form. The session-only selfie promise means the profile is not written to disk.

requirements.source_phrase: When a user adds a selfie, require them to enter their height, weight, and gender
requirements.statement: The measurements dialog offers a height field, a weight field and a gender/fit selector, marks all three required, and shows an error beside the offending field when a value is empty, non-numeric or not positive without closing the dialog
requirements.notes: Field-level error state matters because the form cannot be skipped; the error must say which field and why in the user's terms.

requirements.source_phrase: Include sizing information for each clothing item, such as its length and general size (small, medium, large, etc.).
requirements.statement: Each catalog card shows the item's size label and its length, and the item detail drawer shows a sizing section with every stored size, length, body measurement, height/weight fit range and the one-of-a-kind badge; no item card or drawer shows an empty sizing field
requirements.notes: The card/drawer split keeps the grid scannable and puts the full sizing table in the drawer; the user names length and general size explicitly.

requirements.source_phrase: Include sizing information for each clothing item, such as its length and general size (small, medium, large, etc.).
requirements.statement: Every item returned by GET /api/fitting-room/products carries non-empty sizing: a sizes list (for example S, M, L, XL or One size), a length, named body measurements, a height range, a weight range, an adjustable flag, a one-of-a-kind flag, an available flag and a seller, with values identical for the same id on every call
requirements.notes: The user names length and general size; the remaining fields come from the build description and are needed by the fit filter, the 'May not fit you' warning and the one-of-a-kind badge.

requirements.source_phrase: Include sample sizing details in the placeholder items for now.
requirements.statement: Every seeded placeholder item has sizing details populated: at least one general size or 'One size', a length, at least one body measurement, a height range and a weight range, and the sample catalog contains at least one item flagged one-of-a-kind with its own unique measurements as well as items in the common S/M/L/XL sizes
requirements.notes: Seed coverage, not exact counts; the user says placeholder items so no item may be blank. The one-of-a-kind item is the niche LARP case the user calls out.

requirements.source_phrase: many pieces may be niche, one-off items rather than mass-produced clothing
requirements.statement: An item whose stored one-of-a-kind flag is true shows a 'One of a kind' badge on its catalog card and in its detail drawer, and its sizing is presented as a unique measurement rather than as a manufactured size run
requirements.notes: The badge is visible on the card and in the drawer so the niche status is not buried in detail.

requirements.source_phrase: Users should be able to click each item, remove it, or swap it in and out of the outfit.
requirements.statement: Each row in the outfit list has an open control that opens that item's detail drawer, a remove control that takes the item out of the selection entirely, and a toggle control; operating a control changes the outfit list and the worn set immediately, and a removed item does not appear in the next preview request
requirements.notes: Build names outfit-item-open-{id}, outfit-item-remove-{id} and outfit-item-toggle-{id}; the test should use those testids. 'Click each item' must leave the outfit list reachable after the drawer closes.

requirements.source_phrase: swap it in and out of the outfit
requirements.statement: When a second item in the same category is put on, the first item moves to a set-aside state and remains in the outfit list with a 'Swap in' control while the new item is worn; pressing 'Swap in' puts the first item back on and sets the second aside, and the toggle reads 'Take off' on a worn item and 'Swap in' or 'Put on' otherwise
requirements.notes: Build detail: outfit-item-toggle-{id} shows 'Swap in' and outfit-item-replaces-{id} marks the replaced item. The test should verify the label change as well as the worn set.

requirements.source_phrase: Users should be able to click each item, remove it, or swap it in and out of the outfit.
requirements.statement: The assistant endpoint accepts a benched_ids array alongside equipped_ids and returns remove[] for items the user asks to take off, and the try-on endpoint is called with only the worn item_ids so a benched or removed item is never rendered as worn; no benched or removed id appears in equip or highlight
requirements.notes: Client state alone cannot guarantee the preview corresponds to the visible worn set; the request contract is the server-side half. From the build's 'POST /api/fitting-room/assistant accepts benched_ids and returns remove[]'.

requirements.source_phrase: Also allow users to continue making these changes with voice commands or text.
requirements.statement: A single typed message may contain more than one change (for example 'take off the cowl and put the barbute back on' or 'get rid of the dagger'); the assistant reply names the remove, unequip and equip ids it applied and the outfit list and worn set reflect all of them
requirements.notes: Build feature list gives the exact sample commands; the observable is that every clause in one message is applied, not just the first.

requirements.source_phrase: The Quartermaster should only suggest items available in the marketplace.
requirements.statement: Assistant replies, suggestions and highlights only name items that are currently available in the sample catalog, and every suggested item can be found in the catalog grid and opened from its card
requirements.notes: The user names the assistant Quartermaster; the test should confirm every id in a reply resolves to a visible, available catalog item.

requirements.source_phrase: Every piece shown on the person should correspond to a specific available listing.
requirements.statement: Every item visible on the generated preview corresponds to a worn row in the outfit list and to an available catalog listing, and no generic, leftover or unlisted gear appears on the person
requirements.notes: The visual half of the user's correspondence promise; test by generating with one known item and checking the outfit list and preview agree, not by subjective image judgement alone.

requirements.source_phrase: so the demo can filter clothing
requirements.statement: An 'Only gear that fits me' switch sits with the catalog filters; once measurements are saved it is on by default and the grid shows only items the measurements fit, and turning it off restores every catalog item with its fit warning still visible
requirements.notes: The build makes the switch default-on; the user's 'so the demo can filter clothing' is the promise. The switch must not hide the way back to all items.

requirements.source_phrase: so the demo can filter clothing
requirements.statement: GET /api/fitting-room/products accepts the saved height, weight and gender/fit plus a fits_only flag; with fits_only true it returns only items whose fit range contains the measurements, and with fits_only false it returns every seeded item with a per-item fit boolean, never an item outside the catalog
requirements.notes: The filter belongs on the server so the fit values agree with the size labels and warnings; a client-only filter would let a direct API call return non-fitting gear.

requirements.statement: For a saved profile, an item counts as fitting only when the height lies within the item's stated height range and the weight within its stated weight range, both bounds inclusive, unless the item is adjustable, and the same boolean is returned by products, the item detail and the assistant's candidate list
requirements.notes: Assumption recorded: ranges are inclusive at both ends; an adjustable item still fits only inside its stated range. Derived from the build's 'height and weight range it fits, whether it adjusts'. Exactly-at-the-boundary values are the hard test case.

requirements.statement: Choosing gender/fit in the measurements form sets the catalog's gender filter to the matching value plus unisex, the filter control shows that selection, and changing the selection updates the grid without re-entering the measurements
requirements.notes: From app_summary: 'Choosing men's or women's fit also sets that filter in the catalog.' The user's 'gender so the demo can filter clothing' makes the connection; unisex matching is already in R-043.

requirements.statement: Each catalog card shows a suggested size label for the saved measurements, and that label is always one of the item's declared sizes or 'One size', never a size the item does not offer
requirements.notes: Build says 'shows a size label on each card' and suggests a size. The exact selection algorithm is left to the app; the invariant checked is membership in the item's own sizes.

requirements.statement: A catalog card for an item the server marks as not fitting shows a 'May not fit you' warning while the card remains usable, and a card for an item that fits shows no such warning
requirements.notes: From app_summary: 'a May not fit you warning'. The warning belongs to the paranoid half of the fit filter: items are shown but flagged when the filter is off.

requirements.statement: The item detail drawer's sizing section highlights the user's suggested size among the item's sizes and states whether the item should fit the saved measurements, using the same fit result as the catalog warning
requirements.notes: From app_summary: 'The item details view has a sizing section that highlights the user's size and says whether the item should fit.' The drawer and the card warning must not disagree.

requirements.statement: A measurement tag on the fitting-room screen shows the saved height, weight and gender/fit, and activating its edit control opens the same measurements form pre-filled; saving a changed value updates the tag and the filtered catalog without requiring a new selfie or a new try-on
requirements.notes: From app_summary: 'A tag shows these measurements and lets users edit them.' Editing must not require re-uploading the selfie, otherwise the gate would re-prompt.

requirements.statement: The height field accepts centimetres and feet/inches and the weight field accepts kilograms and pounds; entering 180 cm or 5 ft 11 in saves the same height within 1 cm, and entering 80 kg or 176 lb saves the same weight within 1 lb, with the measurement tag showing the saved value in the unit the user chose
requirements.notes: Unit entry is in the build description, not the user line; conversion assumptions: 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, values rounded to the nearest whole cm/kg for filtering.

requirements.statement: The server stores one canonical height in centimetres and one canonical weight in kilograms, converts ft/in and lb inputs to those units, and the converted value agrees with a direct cm or kg input to within one whole centimetre or one pound
requirements.notes: Calculation rule: 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, rounding to the nearest whole unit. Without a single canonical value the fit filter and try-on could disagree.

requirements.statement: The assistant receives the saved measurements and considers only items whose fit boolean is true; if the model names a non-fitting item, the server removes it from equip and highlight and the reply says which item was skipped or how many were skipped
requirements.notes: From app_summary: 'The AI stylist respects sizing: it only sees items that fit the person; the server removes those picks and the stylist says what it skipped.' The user's fit-filter promise implies the assistant must not suggest gear that does not fit.

requirements.statement: When the assistant skips one or more items because they do not fit the saved measurements, the chat reply visibly says which item or how many items were skipped, rather than silently returning fewer items
requirements.notes: Skipped-without-saying is the failure the agent flags; the user's 'Only gear that fits me' expectations make the omission user-visible.

requirements.statement: POST /api/fitting-room/tryon accepts the saved height, weight and gender/fit and includes them in the provider request; two otherwise identical generations for profiles with clearly different height and weight produce images whose body proportions differ, and each image is still a full-body person wearing the equipped items
requirements.notes: AI content check; cap at two calls because each generation costs credits. The build says the try-on uses measurements for body proportions. 'Clearly different' means e.g. 150 cm/45 kg versus 200 cm/120 kg.

requirements.statement: If the try-on cannot render one of the worn items, the screen names the omitted item or items in the user's terms and the outfit list marks it, instead of showing a preview that silently leaves it out
requirements.notes: Agent's known open issue: 'the try-on silently omits items it cannot find.' The user's 'every piece shown should correspond to a specific available listing' makes a silent omission a failure of correspondence.

requirements.statement: When POST /api/fitting-room/tryon cannot resolve or render a worn item, the response identifies the omitted id or ids in a field the screen shows and does not return a success image that silently drops them; if no item can be rendered it returns an error and no image
requirements.notes: Server half of the omitted-item promise; the agent reports the current build omits silently. The response must still be distinguishable from a successful complete render.

requirements.statement: If the user sends a second chat message before the assistant reply arrives, the message is queued, both replies appear in the order sent, and each reply applies its changes to the state left by the previous reply; no queued message is dropped or answered twice
requirements.notes: Build description: 'Messages sent while assistant is thinking are queued and processed in order.' The user's 'continue making these changes' supports it; test by sending two commands quickly.

requirements.statement: When the 'Only gear that fits me' filter leaves no items, the grid area shows an explicit no-matching-gear message and a control to turn the fit filter off, rather than a blank region or an endless spinner
requirements.notes: Zero-row state of the newly default-on filter; a blank grid could otherwise be read as a broken catalog.

requirements.statement: At 1280px and 390px widths the measurements dialog shows the height, weight and gender inputs and the submit control without clipping or overlapping, and the measurement tag remains visible after the dialog closes
requirements.notes: Tier 2 layout class; the demo is shown on a laptop and a phone, and a clipped submit would trap the user because the dialog cannot be skipped.

requirements.statement: The assistant chat is presented as the Quartermaster, and the surrounding fitting-room copy uses LARP gear, costume and marketplace vocabulary rather than generic fashion or placeholder text
requirements.notes: Product copy and shell; the user names the assistant Quartermaster in the new window.

requirements.statement: The sample catalog contains at least two items in the same category, one marked available and one marked unavailable, so a request for that category can distinguish a suggested listing from an unavailable one
requirements.notes: Testability seed for the availability rule: without an unavailable item the assistant cannot be shown to exclude one. The unavailable item remains a catalog listing with its own id.
